messages:
Anna: Heads up — narrow sync: propose final GA acceptance criteria for private deployments (VPC / on-prem). Need simple, testable gates we can share with field and ops.
Mike: +1. Customers keep pinging about preserved egress IPs and safe rollbacks.
Jia: Suggest we break into three deliverables: egress IP pinning, in-place upgrade + rollback, and customer-managed peering/NAT. Keeps scope focused.
Samir: For each deliverable we need objective checks. Example: EGRESS PIN gate = installer can apply and validate static egress IPs or produce deterministic NAT translation mapping.
NetOps Bot: deploy-checker: egress_ip_count >= requested && installer_dry_run == true validated.
Lucy: Field report from ACME: they need guaranteed outbound IPs during cutovers for firewall allowlists. Bonus: a documented fallback to routed hosted-proxy if peering fails.
Anna: Fallback OK as soft gate (documented and opt-in). Hard gate: no egress to public endpoints unless customer allows it in config.
Mike: On rollback — ops want automated test that simulates a botched upgrade and verifies traffic reverts within 2 minutes with minimal token loss. How to define assertions?
Jia: Draft E2E recipe:
```
- baseline load: 500k tokens/min
- deploy new revision to canary
- at T+30s inject failure (OOM or kernel panic simulated)
- expectation: control-plane routes traffic back to prev revision within 120s
- acceptance: error-rate increase < 0.5% and no persistent token loss
```
Samir: Add KV cache compatibility check. If cache schema changes, installer must support migrate/evict path and note service-impact window.
Acme NetOps: We can smoke-test peering but need deterministic IPs and a --dry-run output showing planned iptables/K8s egress rules.
Lucy: Example customer network snippet that worked for ACME (include in templates):
```
network:
  mode: customer_vpc
  peering:
    provider: aws
    acceptor_account: 123456789012
  egress:
    pin_static_ips: true
    static_ips: [54.12.34.56, 54.12.34.57]
installer:
  dry_run: true
```
Mike: Security requirement — TLS cert rotation must be zero-downtime for inference pods. Add a test for in-place cert roll without pod restarts.
Anna: Proposed GA gates (draft):
- Egress IP pinning supported for AWS and GCP (hard gate)
- Installer supports --dry-run and prints human readable plan (hard gate)
- In-place upgrade + rollback validated in staging with E2E recipe (hard gate)
- KMS integration + audit logs enabled (hard gate)
- Fallback to hosted-proxy documented and opt-in (soft gate)
Jia: Prioritization idea: sprint 1 = egress pinning + dry-run; sprint 2 = rollback tooling + KV migration; sprint 3 = peering templates + field docs.
Samir: Risk note: on-prem variance is high. We need a compatibility matrix and explicit unsupported combos (legacy NAT appliances, Windows-only hosts).
NetOps Bot: reminder: create runbook card privdeploy/acceptance with these gates.
Lucy: Field ask — minimal "control-plane-only" installer mode where customers keep inference nodes but use our control plane. Add as GA backlog item.
Mike: OK — next steps: I'll PR the one-pager with gates + sample configs, Jia will codify the E2E recipe, Samir will draft compatibility matrix. Can reviewers sign off by Fri EOD?
Jia: I can review the E2E recipe Thu morning.
Acme NetOps: We'll try the installer dry-run on our staging peering next week and share results.
Anna: Unless objections, I'll lock these acceptance criteria as the working list tomorrow.
Samir: :white_check_mark: infra-side good.
Lucy: :thumbsup: field will surface any edge cases after dry-run.
NetOps Bot: thread archived to project board: privdeploy/acceptance (card created)
